title: GERMAN LANGUAGE – LEVEL 03
overview: German Language – Level 03 develops pre-intermediate German communication skills, building on the elementary foundation of Levels 01 and 02. Participants learn to sustain conversations about familiar topics, describe experiences and plans, understand connected spoken and written texts, and communicate with greater grammatical accuracy in everyday and routine professional situations. The course integrates guided language study with practical tasks, pronunciation coaching, and ongoing feedback.
audience: Learners who have completed German Language – Level 02 or demonstrate equivalent elementary proficiency.
Professionals and students seeking greater independence in everyday German communication.
Individuals preparing to use German in travel, social interactions, study, or routine workplace settings.
methodology: Interactive instructor-led lessons combining concise grammar explanations with contextual practice.
Pair and group conversations, role-plays, information-gap tasks, and guided discussions.
Listening to authentic-style dialogues and reading short practical texts, followed by comprehension tasks.
Structured writing, pronunciation feedback, vocabulary recycling, and regular formative checks.
Integrated communicative practice and a final skills-based assessment.
competencies: Communicate in connected sentences about familiar experiences, preferences, routines, and plans.
Apply pre-intermediate grammar, word order, and verb forms with increasing accuracy.
Understand the main points of clear speech and accessible written materials on familiar topics.
Write coherent short messages, descriptions, and practical workplace communications.
Use strategies to clarify meaning, ask follow-up questions, and maintain a conversation.
objectives: Narrate past experiences and describe sequences of events using appropriate tense forms.
Discuss intentions, arrangements, preferences, reasons, and simple hypothetical situations.
Use subordinate clauses, modal constructions, case patterns, and adjective endings in context.
Manage everyday service interactions and routine workplace exchanges more independently.
Extract key information from short announcements, conversations, emails, and articles.
Produce organized short texts and deliver a brief prepared oral presentation.
